⚙️ Rules & setup
Players can borrow from the bank (up to the limit) and repay later at this interest rate, from the Manage panel on their turn.
🤝 Alliances
Once this is on, pair players up from the lobby list below (each pair shares one pooled balance — money either of them earns or spends comes out of the same pot — and the whole pair goes bankrupt or wins together).
🏠 Rent
⏳ Turn timer
Shown as a shrinking ring around the active player's avatar. If time runs out, their turn is ended automatically (or the dice are rolled for them if they haven't rolled yet). The clock pauses whenever a player is stuck negative and can't legally end their turn — it picks back up once they're square again.
🔨 Auctions
Owners can also start their own auction on properties they own (no houses, unmortgaged) from the Manage panel, picking their own starting bid and a 3/6/9s timer.
🏗️ Building
🤝 Buy out opponent's properties
🃏 Cards & power-ups
Off (default): a normal board, with Lucky Wheel and Happy Birthday paying out cash. Switch either on and that tile stops paying cash entirely — every landing draws a power-up instead, and the tile itself relabels on the board to show it.
Each power-up below can be switched off entirely, or dialed up/down against the others — the weight is only relative, so it doesn't need to add up to 100.
Property Shield and Rent Doubler are played as buttons on your own turn, once per card drawn — Shield must be raised before you roll and blocks every rent charged to you for the rest of that turn; Rent Doubler is armed whenever you like and doubles every rent you collect from that point until your next turn comes back around. Property Freeze is played on your turn against an opponent's property — for their next 2 turns it can't be built on, sold, mortgaged, or collect rent from anyone. Bankruptcy Insurance is kept in hand and never played by hand — it fires on its own the moment you'd otherwise go bankrupt for good, cancelling that debt once.
🎲 Side bets
A purely social side-game — anyone other than the active player can challenge a quick $25/$50/$100 bet on their upcoming roll (doubles, odd/even, or over/under 7) right up until they roll. Winner takes the wager straight from the loser; it never touches properties, rent, or the bank.
